The '''1999 Decipher World Championship''' was the 4th Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 12–13 November 1999 at [[DecipherCon 1999]] in the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia. [[Gary Carman]] (United Kingdom) defeated [[Steven Lewis]] (United States) 2 (+19) and became the first British World Champion. He won with a Dark [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] deck and a Light [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] deck that he rebuilt after losing his Day 1 decks.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref><ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref><ref name="sw">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128144348/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Star Wars CCG World Championship], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref><ref name="sat">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Lalumiere Saturday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 20 November 2000)</ref> The field was 32 players: 4 Open, 2 Invitational, 23 Regional and 2 Wild Card qualifiers plus the defending champion.<ref name="field">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128125001/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Finalists], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref>

The site was the same Cavalier Hotel that hosted the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]]. [[Kendrick Summers]] announced DecipherCon for the Cavalier Resort and Hotel in Virginia Beach on 27 September 1999.<ref name="rfd26">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Broadcast 26 - Radio Free Decipher], Kendrick Summers (27 September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive]. Watch page: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010122343/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive].</ref>

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Endor]]. [[Enhanced Cloud City]] was not legal in the World Championship decks. Decipher sold that product from 9am Saturday for other convention events, including the Invitational and the Sunday Team Challenge.<ref name="ecc">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128112134/http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/1999/1099/102699storyA.html Star Wars CCG Enhanced Cloud City and the '99 World Championships], Kendrick Summers, Decipher (26 October 1999)</ref>

=== Top 8 bracket ===

There was no elimination bracket: after Day 2 the leader and second-placed player met in a two-game Final Confrontation.<ref name="sw03" /><ref name="trando" />

==== Final Confrontation ====

Lalumiere's live Event Report Board coverage of both games is transcribed on [[1999 Decipher World Championship Final Confrontation]].

The match was Saturday after Day 2. Lewis was the only undefeated in the round of 12 and met Carman.<ref name="sw03" /><ref name="trando" /> [[Kathy Lischke]] announced the two finalists on Decipher's event board.<ref name="kl-final">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$7077-13141$1 "Star Wars: CCG Final Confrontation"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (13 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001025033142/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$7077-13141$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

Game 1: Carman [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (Outer Rim Scout) against Lewis's Clak'dor VII Operative Speeder ([[Local Uprising / Liberation|Local Uprising]]). Carman won by 22.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp CCG World Champion], TheForce.Net (14 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160101143010/http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

Game 2: Carman [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] inserts against Lewis [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down]]. Lewis probed the Hidden Base with Security Precautions. Carman resolved Never Tell Me The Odds for 8 after Grimtaash stripped Torture. Lewis won by 3 with Lateral Damage. Combined, Carman 2 (+19).<ref name="trando" /><ref name="tfn" />

[[Mark Tuttle]] called game 2 the most exciting match he had ever watched. Decipher posted his play-by-play audio of both games.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="sw" /> Francis K. Lalumiere called Carman's win the last World Champion title of the millennium.<ref name="sat" />

Carman's published lists are the rebuilt pair from Friday night. He had lost the decks he used on Day 1.<ref name="trando" /> Lischke's same-day report said he found the decks missing on Saturday morning. He built two new decks with help from another qualifier and had never played them before the final.<ref name="kl-necessity">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 "Necessity is the mother of invention"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (13 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001028020703/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Day 2 ==

Day 2 (four games): [[Yannick Lapointe]] was the early leader; Winkelhaus and Hays took early losses. Lewis was the only undefeated and met Carman in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="trando" />

Official SW.03 scores after four games (Saturday). == Day 1 ==

Day 1 (32 players, eight games): [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] led on 13 (143), then [[Clint Hays]] on 13 (80). Carman finished third on 12 (71) after a strong close. [[Matt Lush]] finished 28th. That evening Carman lost his decks and rebuilt overnight, borrowing and adjusting Markus Wuest's Light.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="final12">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000122170128/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/final12.html They advanced to the Round of 12], Decipher (Wayback 22 January 2000)</ref><ref name="lush">Matt Lush, [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ day-one-world-championships], DeckTech (16 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009094534/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Official SW.02 scores after eight games (Friday). Places 1–32 follow that sheet. [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] led on 13 (143).<ref name="dc99sw02_1">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW02_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 SW World Championships], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001031220826/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW02_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Dark and Light cells are the lists used on Friday; for players who reached the final twelve with the same pair, the deck links are in the Results table.

That evening Carman lost his decks and rebuilt overnight. He borrowed and adjusted Markus Wuest's Light for Saturday.<ref name="trando" />

== Qualifiers ==

Qualification was more exclusive than 1997–1998: one player per region plus Open, Wild Card, and invitational seats. The regional structure drew heavy criticism and was not kept for 2000. [[Joe Alread]] missed the main event for the first time (he won the Ironman side event).<ref name="trando" />

Decipher listed 32 finalists for the World Championship.<ref name="field" /> The field was 4 Open, 2 Invitational, 23 Regional, 2 Wild Card, and the defending champion [[Matt Potter]].<ref name="field" />

== Side events ==

=== Wild Card ===

Thursday 11 November 1999 was the Wild Card, an open tournament at [[DecipherCon 1999]]. The top two advanced to Friday Day 1 of the World Championship. [[John Arendt]] finished first and [[James Lafferty]] finished second.<ref name="rfd112" /><ref name="lafferty-dd" /><ref name="trando" /> Both played Day 1. Lafferty played all three days. [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd.<ref name="iv16">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Internet Archive]</ref> [[Francis Lalumiere]] counted 146 Star Wars players in that event.<ref name="thu">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000903021929/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html Lalumiere Thursday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 3 September 2000)</ref>

Decipher's event page set the Wild Card for 3 p.m., with no final playoff and the event fee covered by convention entry. It would run 6 games (3 rounds) for 64 or fewer players and 8 games (4 rounds) for 65 or more. The top two would stay at the Cavalier Hotel as Decipher's guests (room and meals, travel not reimbursed), and the top 8 would receive trophies.<ref name="wc-events">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/wildcardevents.html DecipherCon event schedule: Star Wars CCG & Star Trek CCG Wild Card Tournaments], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217224533/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/wildcardevents.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Francis K. Lalumiere wrote at 9:10 p.m. that 146 Star Wars players were in that event. Worlds started on Friday.<ref name="thu" /> Decipher's score sheet lists 147 players.<ref name="dc99sw01_1">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 SW Wildcard], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011101231420/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher's thu01 photo caption gives 161.<ref name="thu01">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/THU/thu01.html DecipherCon 1999 photo thu01], Decipher. Caption: "Wild Card players, 161 for Star Wars CCG and 61 for Star Trek CCG, will soon fill the room." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010119074700/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/THU/thu01.html Internet Archive]</ref> Play ran into Friday morning. Decipher wrote that [[James Lafferty]]'s 2nd place was not secured until 1 a.m. Friday.<ref name="lafferty-dd">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000301030330/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/deckdesigns/121099laffertylight.html James Lafferty Light], Decipher Deck Designs (Wayback 1 March 2000)</ref>

[[John Arendt]] finished first.<ref name="rfd112">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=880s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher], Scott Gaeta (25 January 2002), at 14:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref> [[James Lafferty]] finished second.<ref name="lafferty-dd" /> Those two played Day 1 on Friday. [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd; only the top 2 advanced.<ref name="iv16" /> [[Scott Lingrell]] posted an 8–2 record in the Wild Card. [[Christopher Kagehiro]] and [[Stephanie Kagehiro]] played a Game 2 match. [[Kim Caton]] of Philadelphia won Wild Card Game 2.<ref name="lingrell-wc">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/1354 Yavin IVCheese], DeckTech (Scott "CRingwell" Lingrell, 22 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024191350/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/1354/ Internet Archive]</ref>

* [[1999 Decipher World Championship ECC Sealed]] — Sealed Deck (unofficial), 13 November 1999
* Sunday Team Challenge (played with [[Enhanced Cloud City]], which went on sale at 9am Saturday for the convention's other events)<ref name="ecc" />
* Ironman, won by [[Joe Alread]]<ref name="trando" />

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on the article, the article keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* Akesson writes that he placed 7th on Day 1 with 10 (+46); Decipher's round-of-12 list has him 8th on 10 (45), behind James Lafferty on the same score.<ref name="tr-d163">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ world-championships-by-martin-akesson], DeckTech (Martin "Mart" Akesson, 9 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025134508/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* Akesson's game scores give a Day 2 total of 4 (−12); Decipher's SW.03 Day 2 scores have him on 4 (−9).<ref name="tr-d163" />
* Wild Card players: 146 in Lalumiere's Thursday wrap-up,<ref name="thu" /> 147 on Decipher's SW.01 score sheet<ref name="dc99sw01_1" /> and 161 in the thu01 photo caption.<ref name="thu01" />
* Lischke's 13 November board report places Carman's deck rebuild on Saturday morning; the Trandosite interview places it on Friday night.<ref name="kl-necessity" /><ref name="trando" />
